text:
ashwin: seeing a weird pattern — ~20 pods Pending in us-west3 despite warm nodes showing available GPUs. scheduler keeps trying then backing off, then we provision more spot capacity. cost spike this morning :exploding_head:

maria: any recent scheduler config changes?

ashwin: none from our side. noticed a handful of nodes with a stale node-label `shelf-shelter=true` that used to gate tiny-pod placement. pods are small (0.25 GPU) and the scheduler prebind seems to prefer nodes with the label even when they’re full; when it fails it requeues and we end up spinning up extra nodes.

li: can you paste a `kubectl describe pod` + pod events for one of the stuck pods?

ashwin: pasted below (abridged):

```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/train-xyz to node-uw3-12
  Warning  FailedAttach      2m    attach-detach      AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-abc" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
  Warning  FailedScheduling  1m    default-scheduler  Pod failed to fit: 0/10 nodes had available gpu, node(s) had taint: shelf-shelter=true:NoSchedule
```

jonathan: interesting — `shelf-shelter` taint logic dates back to a rack-provisioning experiment. I think scheduler still has an affinity rule that glues tiny pods to those nodes (to keep NVLink locality for larger jobs). that rule may be overzealous now.

ekaterina: if scheduler repeatedly prebinds then fails attach we get a churn loop. can we short-circuit by treating stale taints as soft (NoSchedule->PreferNoSchedule) for a short canary window?

ashwin: proposed quick mitigation: patch scheduler predicate order so we relax `shelf-shelter` hard taint for pods with resource <0.5 GPU. plan: 1) apply hotfix to canary cluster (us-west3-a) 2) monitor Pending count and spot provisioning rate 3) roll to remaining AZs if green.

maria: +1 on canary. metrics to watch: `kube_scheduler_pending_pods`, spot node launch rate, and cost/hour for us-west3. set alert if provisioning rate > baseline * 3 in 15m.

jonathan: I’ll own the patch and rollout. tentative kubectl patch (dry-run):

```
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm scheduler-config --patch '{"data": {"predicateOrder": "...relax-shelf-shelter-for-small-pods..."}}' --dry-run=client -o yaml
```
I’ll submit the PR and tag @maria @ashwin for quick review.

ops-bot: alert created: ALRT-3012 - us-west3 spot provisioning rate high (threshold 3x baseline). linked runbook: /runbooks/spot_scale_surges.md :white_flag:

ashwin: also chasing root cause — need to decide whether to remove the stale taint from nodes (if they’re really free) or change scheduler policy. removing taint is higher risk (affects large-job locality).

ekaterina: can we add a TTL to the `shelf-shelter` taint via a small controller? if label becomes stale for >12h mark it as prefer and notify owners. longer-term fix but avoids human touch.

maria: agreed. short-term canary patch + monitor; medium-term controller for taint TTL. jonathan, deploy canary now and ping pager on regression.

jonathan: deploying canary to us-west3-a in ~10m, will post rollout status here.

ashwin: if the canary doesn’t reduce spot launches we’ll rollback and instead flip the taint to `PreferNoSchedule` on the orphaned nodes as emergency stopgap.

jonathan: canary applied (us-west3-a). logs look clean so far — Pending down from 22 -> 3 in 8m. cost ingress trending down.

maria: nice, leave canary for 30m then promote. opening a ticket to track the controller RFC. thanks team :thumbsup:
